What was done to a series before registration

Source: R/prepare.R
preparation_notes.Rd

Every preparation function (read_hydro_series(), align_series(), convert_units(), fill_gaps(), zero_negatives()) notes what it did on the series it returns. preparation_notes() lists those notes. register_data() writes them into the calibration log, so a reviewer can see, for instance, that 412 steps of evaporation were interpolated and three negative rain values set to zero.

Usage

preparation_notes(x)

Arguments

x

A prepared series, or a data frame of them (such as forcing).

Value

A data frame with columns series, step and detail; no rows if nothing is noted.

Details

Notes travel with a vector through data frames, data.tables, assignment and arithmetic, but subsetting (x[1:100]) drops them: prepare the whole series, then register it.

See also

check_inputs(), register_data()

Examples

rain <- c(0, 1.2, NA, 0.4, -0.1)
rain <- zero_negatives(fill_gaps(rain, "zero", label = "rain"), label = "rain")
preparation_notes(rain)
#>   series      step
#> 1 series      gaps
#> 2 series negatives
#>                                                                                      detail
#> 1 rain: 1 missing steps in 1 gap, longest row 3 for 1 steps; zero, 1 filled, 0 left missing
#> 2                           rain: 1 negative values (smallest -0.1, total -0.1) set to zero
